name: Klondike placers (Bonanza-Eldorado-Hunker-Dominion)
note: ~20 Moz produced since 1896 from creek and White Channel gravels under frozen muck (Yukon Geological Survey)

name: Cariboo placers (Barkerville)
note: ~2.5 Moz from creeks of the Cariboo gold rush (1861)

name: Fairbanks placers
note: ~8 Moz from buried creek gravels under loess and muck

name: Nome beach placers
note: ~5 Moz from modern and raised beach lines (1899 rush)

name: Sierra Nevada Tertiary gravels and river placers
note: ~40 Moz from California placers: Eocene river channels (hydraulic mining) and modern streams (Clark 1970)

name: Victorian alluvials and deep leads (Ballarat-Castlemaine-Bendigo)
note: about a third of Victoria's ~2500 t came from alluvials and basalt-covered deep leads

name: Otago goldfields placers
note: ~8 Moz from Clutha-Shotover placers (1861 rush)

name: Lena goldfields (Bodaibo)
note: ~1500 t produced since 1846 from Bodaibo valley and buried placers (Lenzoloto)

name: Kolyma placers (Susuman-Yagodnoye)
note: ~2500 t from the Kolyma placer belt since 1928

name: Aldan placers
note: Aldan shield placers (1923 rush)

name: Ural placers (Miass and the eastern slope)
note: 19th-century Ural placers (Miass, Berezovsk, Kochkar valleys)

name: Bambuk placers (Faleme and Kenieba)
note: Bambuk, the gold of medieval Ghana and Mali; eluvial and alluvial workings along the Faleme (order of magnitude)

name: Bure placers (upper Niger and Tinkisso)
note: Bure, the main gold source of the Mali empire (Mansa Musa's pilgrimage of 1324)

name: Lobi placers
note: Lobi goldfield on the Black Volta, traded north from the 14th century

name: Akan placers (Pra-Ofin-Birim)
note: Akan alluvial gold of the Gold Coast, traded to Djenne from the 14th-15th century

name: Adola placers
note: southern Ethiopian alluvial gold

name: Nubian wadi placers (Allaqi-Gabgaba)
note: eluvial and wadi gold worked by ancient Egypt and the medieval Beja and Fatimid miners

name: Antioquia placers (Nechi-Cauca)
note: New Granada's colonial gold; dredged in the 20th century

name: Minas Gerais placers (Ouro Preto-Mariana-Sabara)
note: the 18th-century Brazilian gold rush (~800 t), mostly alluvial and eluvial

name: Tapajos garimpos
note: Amazon garimpo placers (order of magnitude)

name: Madre de Dios placers
note: Amazon foreland placers (order of magnitude)

name: Las Medulas
note: Roman hydraulic mining of a Miocene alluvial fan (~5 t); largely worked out
